name: Google Ads Lead Form - Inbound Receiver

nodes.name: Google Lead Webhook
nodes.notes: POST only: Google never sends a GET, and an endpoint that answers GET is a free probe for whether a dealership's key exists. Path is 'google-ads-lead', NOT 'google-ads-lead/:key' -- n8n registers a path-parameter webhook under an internal webhookId prefix, so the clean URL 404s (measured on the box, 7 Sep 2026). The key travels as ?k=. rawBody is ON because Extract And Shape reads item.binary.data: what arrived is evidence and a re-encode is not what arrived. responseMode is 'responseNode' because the status code IS the contract -- Google retries 5XX and permanently discards on 4XX.

nodes.name: Extract And Shape
nodes.notes: Body lifted verbatim from ops/n8n-google-lead-form/extract-and-shape.node.js (the file receiver.test.js runs). Writes nothing, trusts nothing: it answers only 'is this shaped like a Google delivery' and 'which endpoint key is it addressed to'. Do not hand-edit here; edit the .js file.

nodes.name: Shaped Well Enough To Look Up?
nodes.notes: FALSE -> answer the refusal the Code node already chose (404/400), no database call made.

nodes.name: Resolve Endpoint From URL Key
nodes.notes: An unresolvable key produces ZERO rows -- that is the point of the resolver returning a set. alwaysOutputData is on so the empty case still reaches its own branch and is answered deliberately instead of the workflow ending silently with Google holding no answer. NOTE (measured 16 Sep 2026): the function filters on e.status = 'active' AND tenants.status = 'active'. A 'disabled' endpoint resolves to zero rows and therefore answers 403, which Google DISCARDS. Enable the row before pointing Google here. No onError is set (fault = stop) so a PostgREST refusal throws rather than being answered 200.

nodes.name: Endpoint Resolved?
nodes.notes: FALSE -> 403 GOOGLE_KEY_REJECTED, byte-identical to the wrong-secret answer so the endpoint key space cannot be enumerated.

nodes.name: Verify And Redact
nodes.notes: Body lifted verbatim from ops/n8n-google-lead-form/verify-and-redact.node.js. Its OWN input is the resolved endpoint row; the delivery is read back via $('Extract And Shape'). That ordering (resolve, then authenticate) is deliberate: the secret belongs to the endpoint, not the box, so one global key would let any dealer post into any other dealer's pipeline. Reads $env[secret_ref] by a name that came from our own database, never from the request.

nodes.name: Authenticated?
nodes.notes: TRUE covers ACCEPT and ACCEPT_UNPROMOTABLE. FALSE -> the refusal the Code node chose, with its own status: 500 if the fault is ours (secret unset -> Google holds the lead), 403/400 if it is the caller's.

nodes.name: Record Lead Event

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ p_public_key: $json.public_key, p_external_event_id: $json.lead_id, p_origin_verified: 'shared_secret_in_body', p_payload_raw: $json.payload_raw, p_occurred_at: null, p_normalized: $json.normalized_defect === null ? $json.normalized : null }) }}

nodes.notes: p_normalized is sent ONLY when it satisfies the Lead Event contract. Sending a defective one makes the function raise, the workflow answer 5XX, and Google retry forever a delivery that can never succeed because the form simply did not ask for a phone number. SAFE to retry: door one is idempotent on (endpoint, external_event_id) via ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING plus a re-read (migration 20260907190000), so a redelivery returns was_duplicate=true rather than 23505.

nodes.name: Already Have This Lead?
nodes.notes: At-least-once is Google's documented contract, so a redelivery is ordinary. Answered 200 without touching the stored row: re-promoting is safe, re-rejecting is not, and neither is worth the risk.

nodes.name: A Real Customer We Can Reach?
nodes.notes: can_promote is false for is_test=true AND for a normalized defect. Both end without a lead; the phase below says which.

nodes.name: Promote To Lead
nodes.notes: The only path in this workflow that creates a row in leads.

nodes.name: Hold Without Promoting

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ p_event_id: $('Record Lead Event').item.json.event_id, p_phase: $('Verify And Redact').item.json.is_test ? 'QUARANTINED' : 'REJECTED', p_reason: $('Verify And Redact').item.json.is_test ? 'Google Ads test delivery (is_test=true). The delivery was authenticated and is recorded as evidence that the wire works; its fabricated customer is deliberately not promoted.' : ('The form did not collect enough to contact anyone: ' + $('Verify And Redact').item.json.normalized_defect + '. The delivery itself was fine - the lead form is what needs changing.') }) }}

nodes.notes: Two things end here and they are NOT the same. QUARANTINED = Google's own test button: the wire works and that is worth recording, the fabricated customer must never reach the funnel. REJECTED = a real delivery whose form did not collect enough to contact anybody -- a fact about the dealership's form, which should be visible as one rather than promoted and left to rot.

nodes.name: Respond Refusal Before Lookup
nodes.notes: Status comes from the item, so the 4XX/5XX decision stays in the Code node that has the reasons rather than being re-derived here.

nodes.name: Respond Refusal After Lookup
nodes.notes: Carries 500 ENDPOINT_SECRET_NOT_CONFIGURED, 500 ENDPOINT_HAS_NO_SECRET_REF, 403 GOOGLE_KEY_REJECTED and 400 ENDPOINT_IS_NOT_A_GOOGLE_ENDPOINT. The 500s are deliberate: an unconfigured secret must make Google HOLD the lead, not discard a real customer to keep our misconfiguration quiet.

nodes.name: Respond 403 Key Rejected
nodes.notes: Byte-identical to the wrong-secret answer on purpose: telling them apart would let anyone enumerate which endpoint keys exist. Cost: a dealer who mistypes their key sees a silent refusal, visible on Google's own 'send test data' button.

nodes.name: Respond 200 Already Known
nodes.notes: A redelivery of a lead we already hold. Nothing was written the second time.

nodes.name: Respond 200 Lead Created
nodes.notes: A lead row now exists. This is the only response in this workflow that means that.

nodes.name: Respond 200 Recorded Not Promoted
nodes.notes: 200 on purpose. The delivery was fine; the lead is quarantined (test) or rejected (unreachable customer). Answering 4XX would throw away the evidence of a badly configured lead form.
